newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany considers tax changes to fill budget gap.
newsitem.headline: Germany considers tax changes to fill budget gap.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats want to bring forward a plan to tax life insurance premiums in their bid to plug gaps in next year's budget, party sources said on Thursday.

The sources also said they were considering changing the way companies can carry forward losses to pay less tax in profitable years as another measure to fill holes in 1998 state finances and keep Germany within the criteria for Europe's planned single currency.

Finance Minister Theo Waigel is faced with a financing gap of an additional 32 billion marks ($18.5 billion) in the 1998 budget, caused by lower-than-expected tax income and higher social benefit payouts due to record unemployment.

The tax on life insurance and changes for companies that offest a loss against profits in future years was originally planned to take effect in 1999 as part of a comprehensive reform of the tax system.
Details of the changes were not yet clear, the sources said.
They estimated imposing a levy of three percent on life insurance premiums in 1998 would bring in additional income of 3.5 billion marks.
The sources added that junior coalition parter Free Democrats (FDP) had not yet given their backing to the proposals.
